rule: Classify motion by experiential function before removing activity.
why: Reducing temporal competition can also remove the user's meaningful response.
mechanism: Primary semantic/agency motion owns attention; secondary motion supports or releases it.
whenToUse: Several simultaneous motion sources or an artifact undergoing noise reduction.
whenNotToUse: Do not classify every lively behavior as a defect or freeze meaning-bearing motion.
parameters: Role by state, amplitude, temporal priority, shared cause and motion budget.
dependencies: An inventory of motion layers and their semantic function.
implementationPattern: List trigger → response → meaning for each moving layer.
Mark signature, agency, content, atmospheric and redundant roles per state.
Change one competing layer at a time, then compare primary state responses.

goodExample.claim: INBOUND shared cause and motion budgets helped structure one causal input event.

antiExample.claim: VELORUM refinement became more controlled while Human Review found weaker meaningful state response.

tests: Exercise each named control before/after repair.
Inspect primary action amid ambient activity, at rest and in dense regions.
repairStrategy: Restore meaningful control amplitude when repair weakens it.
NOISE REDUCTION MUST NOT DELETE MEANINGFUL MOTION.
cost: Requires before/after inspection; no extra renderer required.

provenance.claim: Candidate operationalization of existing human/technical experiment evidence; transfer unvalidated.
HEG/TEG specification and Human Authority boundary.

transferability: Observed context only; weaker-model and cross-domain transfer TO VALIDATE.
